proofs.proof_tex:
We use the corrected saturated architecture list.  First consider a permitted recursive response architecture on the retained vertices.  Group its mutually independent exogenous sources by their nonempty retained child sets.  For each \(\varnothing\ne C\subseteq W\), let \(U_C\) be the tuple of all original sources having child set \(C\), with the product law inherited from those sources.  Tuples associated with distinct child sets have disjoint original coordinates and therefore remain mutually independent.  Substitute the tuple coordinates into the old structural equations.  For every exogenous realization and every hard intervention, recursive evaluation in topological order gives exactly the old endogenous solution.  Thus \((V,S)\), \((A^b,S^b)\), and every coordinate of \(\zeta(M)\) are unchanged.  An equation depends essentially on the tuple \(U_C\) if and only if it depends essentially on at least one coordinate: one implication follows by changing that coordinate, while for the other one changes two tuples one coordinate at a time and takes the first step at which the output changes.  Hence the minimal structural graph is unchanged.  Sources with no retained child may be discarded.  There are \(2^N-1=H_{\max}\) nonempty subsets of \(W\), which proves the source-count bound within this response language.

Fix a topological order \(\prec\) for any current permitted finite architecture.  Its saturated super-architecture \(T_{\prec}\) contains every old directed input and every old child-set source.  Define each dense response table to ignore every newly added endogenous input.  For a child set absent from the old architecture, give \(U_C\) a one-point law and make every incident table ignore it; for a child set present in the old architecture, retain its law and its old table dependence.  Induction in the order \(\prec\) shows that the structural solution is unchanged under every intervention.  Moreover, each added directed feature and each unused source feature has essentiality polynomial zero, while every old essential feature retains its old positive witness.  By \(\text{lem:essential-feature-iff}\), the actual minimal graph and its selected projection are unchanged.  Thus every old architecture embeds in one saturated architecture indexed only by its order.  There are at most \(N!=A_{\max}\) orders.

We next prove moment reduction.  After source merging, write the independent sources as \(U_1,\ldots,U_H\), where \(H\le H_{\max}\), and define
\[
 F(U_1,\ldots,U_H)=
 \left(
   (\mathbf 1\{V=v,S=1\})_{v\in\Omega_V},
   h(A^b)\mathbf 1\{S^b=1\},
   \mathbf 1\{S^b=1\}
 \right)\in\mathbb R^{m+2}.
\]
By \(\text{def:moment-map}\), \(\mathbb E[F]=\zeta(M)\).  Hold all source laws except that of \(U_k\) fixed, and put
\[
 g_k(u)=\int F(u_1,\ldots,u_{k-1},u,u_{k+1},\ldots,u_H)
             \prod_{r\ne k}dP_r(u_r).
\]
Independence and iterated integration give
\[
 \zeta(M)=\int g_k(u)\,dP_k(u).
\]

We record the elementary barycenter argument used here.  If an integrable random vector \(Y\) takes values in \(\mathbb R^d\), its expectation belongs to the convex hull of at most \(d+1\) values in the essential range of \(Y\).  Indeed, separation places the expectation in the closed convex hull of the essential range.  If it lies on a proper supporting hyperplane, the nonnegative difference between the supporting affine functional and its boundary value has expectation zero and hence vanishes almost surely; restricting to that hyperplane lowers the affine dimension.  Iteration reaches the relative interior of the closed convex hull in the resulting affine space, which is contained in the convex hull itself.  A finite convex representation then exists, and any representation with more than \(d+1\) points has an affine dependence.  Moving its coefficients along that dependence until one coefficient vanishes preserves both their sum and the barycenter.  Repetition leaves at most \(d+1\) points.

Apply this argument with \(d=m+2\) to \(g_k(U_k)\).  There are values \(u_{k,1},\ldots,u_{k,L_k}\), nonnegative weights \(w_{k,r}\), and \(L_k\le m+3=K_{\max}\) such that
\[
 \sum_{r=1}^{L_k}w_{k,r}=1,
 \qquad
 \sum_{r=1}^{L_k}w_{k,r}g_k(u_{k,r})
 =\int g_k(u)\,dP_k(u).
\]
Replacing only \(P_k\) by this discrete law preserves \(\zeta(M)\) and product factorization.  Repeat for \(k=1,\ldots,H\), always using the currently installed laws for the other sources.  Each step preserves the same full vector, so the final vector remains \(\zeta(M)\), and each source has at most \(K_{\max}\) values.  In particular, the shared normalization
\[
 \rho=\sum_{v\in\Omega_V}c_v(M)
\]
is preserved.  After embedding in the saturated order, zero-mass slots pad every source to \(K_{\max}\), and the finite dense table system is among those counted by the corrected \(R_{\max}\).  This reduction preserves moments; it need not preserve a strict inequality \(Z_e>0\).

Finally take \((p_T,\rho)\in\mathfrak F_\delta(\mathcal P,q)\).  A saturated topological order, its deterministic tables, and its mutually independent source-simplex laws define a recursive finite SCM \(M_{T,p_T}\).  The graph-legality stratum gives a \(G\in\mathcal G(\mathcal P)\) with \(\Psi_{T,G}(p_T)\); hence \(\text{lem:essential-feature-iff}\) yields
\[
 G_S(M_{T,p_T})=G.
\]
The remaining fiber constraints give, for every \(v\in\Omega_V\),
\[
 c_v(M_{T,p_T})=\Phi_T(p_T)_{c_v}=\rho q(v),
 \qquad \delta\le\rho\le1,
 \qquad d_{M_{T,p_T}}=\Phi_T(p_T)_d\ge\delta.
\]
Together with \(\text{ass:positive-selected-law}\), these are the member conditions in \(\text{def:admissible-class}\), so \(M_{T,p_T}\in\mathfrak M_\delta(\mathcal P,q)\).  Because \(\delta>0\), division in
\[
 \theta(M_{T,p_T})=\frac{\Phi_T(p_T)_n}{\Phi_T(p_T)_d}
\]
is valid.

Conversely, an enumerated bounded finite SCM satisfying actual selected-MAG legality has a listed order, a listed dense table system, product source masses \(p_T\), and \(\rho=\sum_v c_v\).  Its exact graph sign pattern satisfies one \(\Psi_{T,G}\) by \(\text{lem:essential-feature-iff}\), and selected-law fit plus the two margins place \((p_T,\rho)\) in \(\mathfrak F_\delta(\mathcal P,q)\).  The two inclusions prove the asserted equality of images.  Nothing in this argument turns moment preservation into preservation of strict essentiality, or exogenizes arbitrary latent endogenous structure while preserving actual parent semantics; those are precisely the unresolved legal-lifting issues.

Fix one saturated order and one dense deterministic response-table system.  Let its \(H=H_{\max}\) potential source-mass vectors be \(p_1,\ldots,p_H\); degenerate or absent sources are represented by zero-mass slots.  For each coordinate \(y\) of the moment map, direct summation over source values gives
\[
 \Phi_T(p_T)_y
 =\sum_{u_1,\ldots,u_H}
   a_y(u_1,\ldots,u_H)\prod_{k=1}^H p_k(u_k),
\]
where \(a_y\) is zero or one for a selected cell or the denominator and is either zero or a value of the rational map \(h\) for the numerator.  Hence every moment coordinate is a rational polynomial of degree at most \(H\).  From the definition of \(Z_e\), a directed-feature polynomial uses at most one mass from each source and has degree at most \(H\); a source-feature polynomial uses two masses from its indexed source and at most one from each other source, and therefore has degree at most \(H+1\).  Simplex normalization and nonnegativity, the equations
\[
 \Phi_T(p_T)_{c_v}=\rho q(v)\quad(v\in\Omega_V),
\]
the bounds \(\delta\le\rho\le1\), the inequality \(\Phi_T(p_T)_d\ge\delta\), and the complete sign formula \(\Psi_{T,G}\) form a finite Boolean combination of rational polynomial sign conditions.  Rationality follows from the declared rationality of \(q\), \(\delta\), and \(h\).

Introduce a free variable \(t\) and add
\[
 \Phi_T(p_T)_n-t\Phi_T(p_T)_d=0.
\]
All response masses and \(\rho\) lie in one existential block.  Strict conditions \(Z_e>0\) and equalities \(Z_e=0\) are retained, so projection gives the actual branch, not its closure.  The disjunction over graphs in \(\mathcal G(\mathcal P)\) is part of the Boolean formula and its atomic predicates are included in \(s_{\mathrm{count}}\).

By the corrected architecture construction, there is one saturated super-architecture for each topological order and therefore at most \(A_{\max}=N!\) choices.  For a fixed order, every potential source has \(K_{\max}\) slots and each vertex table accepts all earlier endogenous inputs and all \(2^{N-1}\) potential sources incident to it.  Direct multiplication over these input configurations is exactly the corrected definition of \(R_{\max}\), so at most \(R_{\max}\) table systems occur per order.

Apply \(\text{lem:one-block-semialgebraic-elimination}\) to each table formula, or to their finite disjunction after counting its atoms in \(s_{\mathrm{count}}\).  It returns an exact quantifier-free sign formula in \(t\) defining the attainable target values of the bounded compiler.  If that formula is false everywhere, the compiler is INFEASIBLE.  Otherwise the target set is bounded.  Indeed, \(h_-\le h(A^b)\le h_+\) pointwise and \(d\ge\delta>0\), so
\[
 h_-d\le n\le h_+d,
 \qquad h_-\le \frac nd\le h_+.
\]
Every boundary point of a one-dimensional rational semialgebraic set is a root of one of the finitely many output polynomials, unless it is one of the explicitly included rational bounds \(h_-\) or \(h_+\).  Standard signed-remainder evaluation, which is part of the Thom-encoding representation in the cited elimination result, isolates and orders those roots.  Thus the infimum and supremum are real algebraic and are isolated exactly, whether or not they are attained.

Let \(t_0\) be either isolated closure endpoint.  Represent it by its square-free polynomial, rational isolating interval, and Thom signs.  Substitution works over the resulting ordered real algebraic coefficient field.  If \(\mathsf{Lift}(t_0)\) is true, \(\text{lem:semialgebraic-sign-sample-points}\) supplies a real-univariate sample point satisfying one Boolean branch.  Its sign table verifies the simplex, moment, margin, and strict essential-feature conditions.  By \(\text{lem:essential-feature-iff}\), the latter verify the actual selected MAG.  The sample point, together with the encoding of \(t_0\), is the positive \(\mathsf{Cert}(t_0)\).

If \(\mathsf{Lift}(t_0)\) is false, the one-block elimination output and its exact sign determinations evaluate to false for every enumerated order, table system, and allowed graph branch.  Recording these finite sign data gives a checkable negative \(\mathsf{Cert}(t_0)\).  It certifies only that the endpoint has no representative in the bounded finite compiler.  It cannot exclude an equal-moment representative among arbitrary SCMs, because that stronger implication is the unresolved open-ended question.  If desired, one may refine the same branch formulas by cylindrical algebraic decomposition into sign-invariant cells, but that optional expansion is not used in the following bound.

For one table formula, the two cited critical-point and block-elimination results give
\[
 (s_{\mathrm{count}}D_{\mathrm{deg}})^{O(p_{\mathrm{dim}})}
\]
ring operations.  Their integer-coefficient estimate bounds intermediate and output bit lengths by \(\tau_{\mathrm{eff}}D_{\mathrm{deg}}^{O(p_{\mathrm{dim}})}\).  Exact integer and algebraic-number arithmetic therefore changes the displayed ring-operation count by a factor polynomial in \(\tau_{\mathrm{eff}}\), with the remaining degree growth absorbed into the singly exponential factor.  Multiplication by at most \(A_{\max}R_{\max}\) enumerated order-table branches yields
\[
 A_{\max}R_{\max}
 (s_{\mathrm{count}}D_{\mathrm{deg}})^{O(p_{\mathrm{dim}})}
 \operatorname{poly}(\tau_{\mathrm{eff}}).
\]
This proves the procedure, its scoped positive and negative certificates, and the claimed intrinsic singly exponential bound.

added_lemmas.statement: Let a family of at most \(s_{\mathrm{count}}\) polynomials of degrees at most \(D_{\mathrm{deg}}\) be given in \(p_{\mathrm{dim}}\) real variables.  There is a critical-point algorithm that computes real-univariate sample-point representations meeting every semialgebraically connected component of every realizable sign condition, together with the signs at those points, using \((s_{\mathrm{count}}D_{\mathrm{deg}})^{O(p_{\mathrm{dim}})}\) ring operations.

proposed.name: Saturated order-indexed response architecture list
proposed.construction: For each topological order \(\prec\) on \(W\), form one saturated super-architecture \(T_{\prec}\).  It contains every directed input slot \(i\to j\) with \(i\prec j\) and one potential independent source \(U_C\) for every nonempty \(C\subseteq W\), incident to every \(j\in C\).  Absence of a directed input or source incidence is encoded by the corresponding equality \(Z_e=0\); activity is encoded by \(Z_e>0\).  Thus there are at most \(A_{\max}=N!\) labeled super-architectures.  Give every potential source at most \(K_{\max}=m+3\) slots, including zero-mass slots, and enumerate every dense deterministic response table; the number of table systems for one order is at most \(R_{\max}\).  For each table system retain precisely the essential-feature sign patterns whose selected latent projection is a graph \(G\in\mathcal G(\mathcal P)\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: One saturated super-architecture per order subsumes every choice of directed slots and child-set sources.

proposed.name: Exact graph-legality stratum in a saturated order
proposed.construction: For a saturated ordered super-architecture \(T\), a graph \(G\in\mathcal G(\mathcal P)\), and source masses \(p_T\), declare the primitive feature \(e\in\mathcal I_T\) active exactly when \(Z_e(T,p_T)>0\), and absent exactly when \(Z_e(T,p_T)=0\).  Apply the finite latent-and-selection projection to this active-feature graph.  The formula \(\Psi_{T,G}(p_T)\) is the disjunction of precisely those complete sign patterns whose projection equals \(G\).  The table comparisons in every \(Z_e\) range over all endogenous inputs, including inputs outside observational support.

proposed_core_edits.reason: In a saturated super-architecture, actual sparse structure is determined by the complete essential-feature sign pattern rather than by pre-enumerated formal slots.

proposed.name: Certified finite legality procedure
proposed.construction: Generate the at most \(N!\) saturated ordered super-architectures, enumerate their dense deterministic table systems, expand every coordinate of \(\Phi_T\) and every \(Z_e\) as a rational polynomial, and introduce \(t\) through \(\Phi_T(p_T)_n-t\Phi_T(p_T)_d=0\).  Form \(\mathsf{Lift}(t)\) as the finite disjunction over table systems and \(G\in\mathcal G(\mathcal P)\).  A one-block existential semialgebraic elimination algorithm based on critical points computes an exact univariate sign description of the attainable \(t\)-set and isolates its algebraic infimum and supremum when it is nonempty.  At each isolated closure endpoint it decides \(\mathsf{Lift}(t)\).  The certificate \(\mathsf{Cert}(t)\) is a Thom-encoded real-univariate sample point for a satisfying branch, or the exact block-elimination sign data showing that every bounded finite branch is empty.  A sign-invariant cylindrical decomposition may optionally expand the latter data, but is not used for the intrinsic complexity bound.

open_obligations.what_is_open: For a positive but potentially unfaithful selected law \(q\), prove or refute that every arbitrary admissible moment vector and every limit of bounded exact-graph moment vectors has an equal-moment representative in the bounded fiber with actual selected MAG in \(\mathcal G(\mathcal P)\).
open_obligations.obstruction: The selected-cell and intervention moments are separately linear in each source law, whereas \(Z_{\operatorname{src}(C,j)}\) is quadratic in its own source law.  Even inside a saturated super-architecture, exact barycentric preservation can delete the last positive witness on a proper face, and the frozen assumptions impose neither faithfulness nor a minimum essentiality margin.  Exogenizing hidden endogenous structure must also preserve actual functional parents rather than only a permitted latent projection.
open_obligations.attempted: Saturating every order removes combinatorial architecture maximality but not the nonlinear witness obstruction.  Adding directed-feature indicators to the barycentric vector preserves those separately linear features, but not the two-copy source-feature polynomials.  Prescribing positive witness atoms is incompatible with an arbitrary boundary barycenter.  The positive exclusive-or support-deletion family demonstrates failure of naive compression, although an equal-moment legal lift repairs that example.  The compelled-collider test closes only for the isolated-selection-root subcase recorded below.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The mandatory collider test closes for the following nontrivial subcase.  Let \(V=\{X,Y,Z\}\) be binary, let the retained structural graph be \(X\to Z\leftarrow Y\) with \(S\) an independent selection root, take \(B=\{X\}\), and assume the positive selected law \(q\) obeys the collider Markov restriction \(X\mathbin{\perp\!\!\!\perp}Y\).  Put
\[
 p_{xy}=q(Z=1\mid X=x,Y=y)\in(0,1).
\]
Choose independent \(U_X,U_Y\) with laws \(q_X,q_Y\), an independent \(U_Z\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\), and measurable sets \(E_{xy}\subset[0,1]\) with Lebesgue measure \(p_{xy}\).  The four sets can be chosen so that \(E_{0y}\ne E_{1y}\) modulo null sets for at least one \(y\), and \(E_{x0}\ne E_{x1}\) modulo null sets for at least one \(x\): begin with intervals of the prescribed lengths, and whenever an equality remains, exchange two sufficiently short subintervals between the set and its complement.  Positivity \(0<p_{xy}<1\) makes each exchange possible, and finitely many disjoint exchanges preserve distinctions already installed.  Define
\[
 X=U_X,\qquad Y=U_Y,\qquad Z=\mathbf 1\{U_Z\in E_{XY}\}.
\]
Then
\[
 \Pr(X=x,Y=y,Z=z)=q_X(x)q_Y(y)q(z\mid x,y)=q(x,y,z),
\]
and the two strict symmetric differences make both arrows into \(Z\) actual functional dependencies, even when \(q\) is unfaithful to one or both arrows.  Taking an independent \(S\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\rho)\), with \(\rho\in[\delta,1]\), gives \(c_v=\rho q(v)\) and \(d=\rho\).  For every bounded binary outcome map \(h\), truncated factorization gives the single attainable selected-intervention value
\[
 \theta=
 \sum_{y\in\{0,1\}}q_Y(y)
 \bigl[h(0)(1-p_{by})+h(1)p_{by}\bigr].
\]
It is attained by the exact collider construction above.  Thus the exact-graph fiber and all its support-stratum closure points lift in this isolated-selection compelled-collider case.  This does not cover selected MAGs in which \(S\) has parents or latent ancestors, nor does it preserve an arbitrary pair \((n,d)\) beyond the value fixed by this collider factorization.

prose_updates.tldr: The note constructs a bounded finite graph-legal response fiber using at most \(N!\) saturated order-indexed super-architectures.  Essential-feature signs encode absent and active arrows and sources, and one-block real-algebraic procedures return endpoint witnesses or certificates excluding a value from every bounded branch with singly exponential dependence on the response-program dimension.  These certificates concern only the bounded finite image: equality with the arbitrary-SCM fiber, closure, and universal endpoint attainment remain open for positive, potentially unfaithful selected laws.  Independently of graph restrictions, consistency and the two calibrated \(\delta\)-margins give a universal closed-form outer envelope; one-source exact complete-COPAG models attain it, so every permitted-graph class containing those witnesses inherits the exact interval.  The binary law \(q=(1,2,3,4)/10\) at \(\delta=1/4\) yields \([1/20,39/40]\) as an audit instance for the survivor-selected cardiac-surgery analysis of Lee et al., not as the headline.

project_justification.gap: Chen and Mooij give a sound-and-complete COPAG identification algorithm on specified model classes; Yang et al. optimize over faithful no-selection PAG-compatible SCMs; Duarte et al. optimize a fixed canonical DAG; and Carey et al. characterize normalized selected-marginalized models. None settles whether the exact actual-parent COPAG fiber for a positive, potentially unfaithful selected law is closed or has attained endpoints. This note also leaves that general question open, while formalizing it and proving bounded-finite and saturated special-case results.
project_justification.niche: The tractable object constructed here is the bounded finite graph-legal response fiber, a finite union of semialgebraic strata. Its essential-feature signs determine the exact selected MAG, and real-algebraic procedures decide whether a boundary value of this bounded image has a legal representative or is excluded from all bounded branches. Equality with, and closure or attainment of, the full arbitrary-SCM fiber remain exactly \(\text{oeq:universal-legal-lifting}\).
project_justification.fill: The project supplies an invariant essential-feature index and if-and-only-if legality test, embeds sparse response models into at most \(N!\) saturated ordered super-architectures, and gives a singly exponential one-block certificate procedure for the bounded finite image.  It proves a graph-independent universal selection-margin envelope with attained one-source endpoints in the exact complete-COPAG subclass, designates the compelled-collider case as the first unresolved kill test for universal lifting, and retains finite-sample confidence-fiber coverage without asserting endpoint convergence.

prose_updates.related_work: Richardson and Spirtes define maximal ancestral graphs under latent marginalization and selection conditioning.  Evans canonicalizes margins of latent DAGs and relates latent projection to intervention, but this does not preserve an exact functional-essentiality stratum under moment compression.  Rosset, Gisin, and Wolfe give network hidden-variable cardinality bounds; their sourcewise reduction motivates the finite support step but does not preserve strict actual-edge witnesses.  Duarte et al. fix a canonical DAG and optimize over graph-permitted finite NPSEMs, without requiring every displayed edge to remain functionally essential.  Yang et al. treat faithful no-selection PAG-compatible SCMs; their edge semantics and the actual-parent, potentially unfaithful selected-MAG semantics here are generally incomparable.  Carey et al. characterize normalized selected-marginalized models, whereas the present margins constrain absolute natural and interventional selection probabilities.  Chen and Mooij give a sound-and-complete COPAG identification algorithm or calculus on specified classes and distinguish \(\mathcal M(G)\) from the positive discrete class \(\mathcal M_d^+(\mathcal P)\); positivity of the selected observed law \(q\) here is not equated with all positivity conditions defining \(\mathcal M_d^+(\mathcal P)\).  Boeken, Forr\'e, and Mooij establish openness and density of faithful laws, which does not supply an equal-moment lift at an unfaithful boundary.  Chernozhukov, Hong, and Tamer, Imbens and Manski, and Chang, Guo, and Malinsky motivate confidence-set inversion, while the formal inference result here is only finite-sample outer coverage.  Lee et al. are the clinical consumer: their survivor-conditioned cardiac-surgery analysis uses FCI and LV-IDA under acknowledged selection bias and graph ambiguity.
prose_updates.interpretation: The closed-form envelope is a universal partial-identification statement derived from consistency, selected-law fit, bounded outcomes, and the two calibrated selection margins; graph assumptions enter only when proving endpoint attainment by a permitted witness subclass.  By contrast, the algebraic endpoint procedure characterizes the bounded finite graph-legal image exactly.  A positive certificate is an attained bounded-model mechanism, while a negative certificate says only that every bounded branch fails and must not be reported as nonattainment over arbitrary SCMs.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: Saturated order-indexed super-architectures eliminate redundant subset enumeration, but they do not close the legality topology.  In the positive binary exclusive-or family, moment-preserving support deletion can send a shared-source essentiality polynomial to zero while holding the selected law and intervention moment fixed.  An equal-moment legal lift exists in that example, so it is a warning against naive compression rather than a negative answer.  More generally, a bounded-compiler exclusion certificate does not exclude a repair outside the finite support bound.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Established results cover child-set source merging within the retained-variable response language, moment-preserving sourcewise finite support on a fixed permitted architecture, embedding into at most \(N!\) saturated ordered super-architectures, exact polynomial legality for bounded finite response models, singly exponential existential-semialgebraic endpoint certification for that bounded image, a universal selection-margin outer envelope with exact complete-COPAG subclass attainment, and finite-sample confidence-fiber event inclusion.  Equality between arbitrary selected SCMs and the bounded compiler, preservation of exact actual-parent semantics through arbitrary canonicalization or compression, and closure or attainment of the full positive-unfaithful COPAG fiber remain open.  No general endpoint-convergence claim is made.  The interval \([1/20,39/40]\) is a binary audit instance; it is not evidence for universal lifting.

statement_notes.justification: This remains the sole nonroutine topological bottleneck between exact actual-parent graph semantics and attained extrema for the full arbitrary-SCM fiber.
statement_notes.gap: The isolated-selection compelled-collider subcase has a legal lift, but neither faithfulness-density results nor saturated finite architecture enumeration settles selected graphs with latent or selection ancestry.
statement_notes.consumer: Its resolution determines whether arbitrary-SCM selection-COPAG bounds may be reported as attained; until then, only bounded-image certificates and subclass attainment have that interpretation.

statement_notes.justification: The compiler gives a maximal finite response language with one saturated super-architecture per order while keeping moment reduction logically separate from graph-legal lifting.
statement_notes.consumer: It supplies an auditable candidate model language for the Lee et al. FCI and LV-IDA setting without treating the candidate language as the full SCM class.

statement_notes.justification: The procedure provides exact endpoint membership or bounded-branch exclusion data at singly exponential one-block complexity.
statement_notes.consumer: The reported certificate can distinguish an attained bounded-model mechanism from a bounded-compiler closure artifact, while its scope warning prevents extrapolation to arbitrary SCMs.

proofs.proof_tex:
Put
\[
 I_b=\{v\in\Omega_V:B(v)=b\},\qquad
 R_- =\sum_{v\in I_b}q(v)\{h(A(v))-h_-\},\qquad
 R_+ =\sum_{v\in I_b}q(v)\{h_+-h(A(v))\}.
\]
Finiteness of \(\Omega_A\) implies that \(h_-\) and \(h_+\) are attained, and their definitions imply \(R_-\geq0\) and \(R_+\geq0\).
Moreover,
\[
 U_\delta-L_\delta
 =(h_+-h_-)\left\{1-\delta\sum_{v\in I_b}q(v)\right\}\geq0,
\]
because \(0<\delta\leq1\) and \(\sum_{v\in I_b}q(v)\leq1\).  Thus the displayed envelope is a nonempty closed interval.

We first prove the graph-free outer bound promised in the maximality audit.  Let \(M\) be any recursive SCM satisfying \(c_v(M)=\rho q(v)\) for every \(v\), \(\delta\leq\rho\leq1\), and \(d_M\geq\delta\); no restriction on \(G_S(M)\) is used in this paragraph.  Since \(\delta>0\), the intervention-selection-margin assumption gives \(d_M\geq\delta>0\), so \(\theta(M)=n_M/d_M\) is well defined.  If \(v\in I_b\), recursive consistency gives
\[
 \{V=v,S=1\}\subseteq\{A^b=A(v),S^b=1\}.
\]
Indeed, order the endogenous variables topologically.  On \(\{V=v,S=1\}\), replacing the equations for \(B\) by the already realized value \(b\) leaves the values of \(B\) unchanged; induction along the remaining structural equations then leaves every later endogenous value, including \(A\) and \(S\), unchanged.  The events \(\{V=v,S=1\}\), \(v\in I_b\), are disjoint.  Hence nonnegativity of \(h(A^b)-h_-\), consistency, selected-law fit, and the population-selection margin yield
\[
\begin{aligned}
 n_M-h_-d_M
 &=\mathbb E_M\!\left[\{h(A^b)-h_-\}\mathbf 1\{S^b=1\}\right]\\
 &\geq \sum_{v\in I_b}\{h(A(v))-h_-\}\Pr_M(V=v,S=1)\\
 &=\rho R_-\\
 &\geq\delta R_-.
\end{aligned}
\]
Because \(d_M\) is a probability, \(0<d_M\leq1\).  Therefore
\[
 \theta(M)-h_-=\frac{n_M-h_-d_M}{d_M}
 \geq\frac{\delta R_-}{d_M}\geq\delta R_-,
\]
which is \(\theta(M)\geq L_\delta\) by the definition of the saturated envelope.  Applying the same argument to the nonnegative map \(h_+-h\) gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 h_+d_M-n_M
 &=\mathbb E_M\!\left[\{h_+-h(A^b)\}\mathbf 1\{S^b=1\}\right]\\
 &\geq\sum_{v\in I_b}\{h_+-h(A(v))\}\Pr_M(V=v,S=1)\\
 &=\rho R_+\geq\delta R_+,
\end{aligned}
\]
and thus
\[
 h_+-\theta(M)=\frac{h_+d_M-n_M}{d_M}
 \geq\frac{\delta R_+}{d_M}\geq\delta R_+.
\]
Consequently \(\theta(M)\leq U_\delta\).  We have proved the universal, graph-independent implication
\[
 c_v(M)=\rho q(v),\quad \delta\leq\rho\leq1,
 \quad d_M\geq\delta
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 L_\delta\leq\theta(M)\leq U_\delta. \tag{1}
\]

We next construct exact complete-COPAG witnesses.  Choose \(a_- ,a_+\in\Omega_A\) with \(h(a_-)=h_-\) and \(h(a_+)=h_+\).  Since \(|\Omega_B|\geq2\), choose \(b^\dagger\in\Omega_B\setminus\{b\}\).  Let a single exogenous source \(U\) have one state \(u_v\) for each \(v\in\Omega_V\), with
\[
 \Pr(U=u_v)=\delta q(v).
\]
If \(\delta<1\), add one state \(u_0\) of mass \(1-\delta\); if \(\delta=1\), omit it.  Strict positivity of \(q\) shows that every displayed \(u_v\) has positive mass, and the total mass is
\[
 \sum_{v\in\Omega_V}\delta q(v)+(1-\delta)=1.
\]
Thus an endpoint model has at most \(m+1\) positive-mass source states, which are its response types.

Place all vertices of \(B\) first in a recursive order, the vertices of \(V\setminus B\) next, and \(S\) last.  For every \(u_v\), set the natural value of the vector \(B\) to \(B(v)\); when \(u_0\) exists, set its natural value to \(b^\dagger\).  For every \(X\in V\setminus B\), use a response table \(f_X(B,U)\) and impose the factual entries
\[
 f_X(B(v),u_v)=X(v).
\]
Impose \(f_S(B(v),u_v)=1\), impose \(f_S(b^\dagger,u_0)=0\) when \(u_0\) exists, and impose
\[
 f_S(b,u)=1
 \quad\text{for every positive-mass state }u. \tag{2}
\]
For the lower endpoint, complete the intervention entries of every coordinate of \(A\) so that
\[
 A(b,u_v)=
 \begin{cases}
 A(v),&B(v)=b,\\
 a_-,&B(v)\neq b,
 \end{cases}
 \qquad A(b,u_0)=a_- \quad(\delta<1). \tag{3-}
\]
For the upper endpoint use the same prescription with \(a_+\) in place of \(a_-\):
\[
 A(b,u_v)=
 \begin{cases}
 A(v),&B(v)=b,\\
 a_+,&B(v)\neq b,
 \end{cases}
 \qquad A(b,u_0)=a_+ \quad(\delta<1). \tag{3+}
\]
There is no conflict between the factual and intervention entries: when \(B(v)=b\), the first case in \((3-)\) and \((3+)\) is exactly the factual entry, while every altered entry has natural \(B(v)\neq b\); also \(b^\dagger\neq b\).  Fill every still unspecified table entry arbitrarily.  These finite tables define recursive SCMs with one exogenous source.

In either endpoint SCM, precisely the \(u_v\)-types are selected under their natural treatment.  Therefore, for every \(v\in\Omega_V\),
\[
 c_v(M)=\Pr_M(V=v,S=1)=\delta q(v),\qquad \rho=\delta. \tag{4}
\]
Equations \((2)\), \((3-)\), and \((3+)\) imply that every positive-mass type is selected under \(\operatorname{do}(B=b)\), so
\[
 d_M=1\geq\delta. \tag{5}
\]
For the lower model, partitioning the source states according to whether their natural \(B\)-value equals \(b\) gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 n_M
 &=\delta\sum_{v\in I_b}q(v)h(A(v))
   +\left\{1-\delta\sum_{v\in I_b}q(v)\right\}h_-\\
 &=h_-+\delta\sum_{v\in I_b}q(v)\{h(A(v))-h_-\}=L_\delta.
\end{aligned} \tag{6-}
\]
The analogous calculation for the upper model is
\[
\begin{aligned}
 n_M
 &=\delta\sum_{v\in I_b}q(v)h(A(v))
   +\left\{1-\delta\sum_{v\in I_b}q(v)\right\}h_+\\
 &=h_+-\delta\sum_{v\in I_b}q(v)\{h_+-h(A(v))\}=U_\delta.
\end{aligned} \tag{6+}
\]
By \((5)\), these numerators are also the corresponding values of \(\theta(M)\).

It remains to verify exact graphical legality.  Fix \(X\in V\).  If \(X\in B\), the hypothesis \(|\Omega_X|\geq2\) and full support of \(q\) provide positive-mass states \(u_v,u_{v'}\) at which the natural response of \(X\) differs.  If \(X\notin B\), choose \(v,v'\) with \(B(v)=B(v')\), with all desired remaining coordinates fixed, and with \(X(v)\neq X(v')\); such cells exist and their source states have positive mass because every observed state space has at least two elements and \(q\) is strictly positive on \(\Omega_V\).  The factual table constraints then give
\[
 f_X(B(v),u_v)=X(v)\neq X(v')=f_X(B(v),u_{v'}).
\]
Thus \(U\) is a functional-essential source parent of every observed vertex, with the other endogenous inputs held fixed, exactly under the actual-parent convention defining \(G_S(M)\).  For every distinct \(X,Y\in V\), the latent-fork path \(X\leftarrow U\to Y\) is consequently present and remains open given \(S\) and any subset of \(V\setminus\{X,Y\}\), because its only nonendpoint, \(U\), is an unconditioned noncollider.  Maximal projection therefore makes every pair \(X,Y\) adjacent.  Hence the selected MAG on \(V\) has complete skeleton.  Every complete-skeleton selected MAG has the empty conditional-independence model: its length-one path between any two vertices remains open under every admissible conditioning set.  It is therefore in the equivalence class represented by the complete all-circle COPAG.  We have proved
\[
 G_S(M)\in\mathcal G(\mathcal P). \tag{7}
\]
Equations \((4)\), \((5)\), and \((7)\) place both endpoint SCMs in \(\mathfrak M_\delta(\mathcal P,q)\).

For \(t\in(0,1)\), take disjoint copies of the lower and upper source states and multiply their masses by \(1-t\) and \(t\), respectively; use the corresponding response tables on each copy.  For \(t=0\) or \(t=1\), use the relevant endpoint model.  The resulting \(M_t\) is again a one-source recursive SCM.  Equations \((4)\) and \((5)\) remain true after mixing.  The essential-source argument proving \((7)\) remains true on each positive-mass component.  Linearity of the numerator and \(d_{M_t}=1\) give
\[
 \theta(M_t)=(1-t)L_\delta+tU_\delta. \tag{8}
\]
Thus \((8)\) attains every point between the endpoints, while \((1)\) excludes every point outside them.  It follows that
\[
 \Theta_\delta(\mathcal P,q)=[L_\delta,U_\delta].
\]
Moreover, the proof establishes the stronger sandwich transfer: for any family \(\mathscr C\) of recursive SCMs that satisfies the three premises on the left side of \((1)\) and contains all the witnesses \(M_t\),
\[
 \{\theta(M_t):0\leq t\leq1\}
 \subseteq\{\theta(M):M\in\mathscr C\}
 \subseteq[L_\delta,U_\delta],
\]
so its intervention-value image is also exactly \([L_\delta,U_\delta]\).  In particular, this applies to every broader permitted-graph class containing the complete-COPAG witnesses.  This transfer uses no additional graph claim in the outer-bound direction.

If \(h\) is constant, then \(h_-=h_+\) and
\[
 n_M=\mathbb E_M[h_-\mathbf 1\{S^b=1\}]=h_-d_M,
\]
so \(\theta(M)=h_-\) for every compatible model.  The construction above supplies a compatible model, and hence the fiber is \(\{h_-\}\).

Finally suppose the intervention is vacuous, so its submodel equals the factual model.  Selected-law fit and \(\sum_vq(v)=1\) imply
\[
 d_M=\Pr_M(S=1)=\sum_vc_v(M)=\rho
\]
and
\[
 n_M=\sum_{v\in\Omega_V}h(A(v))c_v(M)
 =\rho\sum_{v\in\Omega_V}q(v)h(A(v)).
\]
The population margin gives \(\rho\geq\delta>0\), so division is valid and every compatible SCM has
\[
 \theta(M)=\sum_{v\in\Omega_V}q(v)h(A(v)). \tag{9}
\]
Nonemptiness in the complete-COPAG case follows directly by taking source states \(u_v\) of mass \(\delta q(v)\), an additional unselected state of mass \(1-\delta\) when \(\delta<1\), and making the common source essential for every observed vertex as above.  Thus \((9)\) is the asserted singleton fiber.
